t: Minimizing Array After Replacing Pairs With Their Product
o: We may merge adjacent elements x,y into x*y whenever x*y <= k, and want the shortest achievable array. In example 1 ([2,3,3,7,3,5], k=20) we merge greedily from the left while products stay small, ending with length 3. In example 2 no adjacent pair has product <= 6, so nothing changes and the answer is 4. With n up to 1e5 we need better than exponential search, but note that any merged group's product either stays <= k or becomes unusable, and since values multiply, a window's product exceeds k after at most log2(k)+1 multiplications (or hits a 0). This bounds how far left we must look.
k: DP over prefixes: dp[i] = min length achievable for the first i elements.
When extending to index i, only windows whose product is <= k matter, and such windows have length O(log k) unless a 0 appears (product 0 is always allowed).

a.n: Approach 1: Prefix DP with bounded backward scan
a.i: Let dp[i] be the minimum length of the array formed from nums[0..i-1]. The last block of the final array is some contiguous window nums[j..i-1] whose product is <= k (a single element is a window of length 1). We scan j backwards accumulating the running product and stop as soon as it exceeds k (unless it became 0, which never exceeds k). Each dp[i] depends only on earlier dp values, giving an O(n log k)-style algorithm because nonzero products double at least every step past the first factor > 1.
s: For each i, set dp[i]=dp[i-1]+1 (element stands alone).
Scan j=i down to 1, maintaining running product p of nums[j-1..i-1]; break when p>k (and p!=0).
Whenever p<=k, relax dp[i] with dp[j-1]+1.
a.t: O(n log k) expected — the backward scan stops once the running product exceeds k, which happens within O(log k) steps for values > 1.

w: The DP is the clean interview answer; mention that zeros act as 'free' merge anchors since product 0 is always <= k. Pitfalls: overflowing products (use early break / 64-bit), and forgetting that a single element needs no operation. A follow-up might ask to reconstruct the actual merges — keep parent pointers in dp.
